why: I compared the builder brief with the verifier brief's checks. The builder brief gives the same inputs and expected outputs that the verifier's Check 1 probe runs: "padLeft('42', 5, '0') === '00042', padLeft('ab', 4) === '  ab'". The verifier's script tests p('42',5,'0') and p('ab',4) and requires "00042" and "  ab". Step 4 repeats these as test cases ('42', 5, '0' -> '00042'; 'ab', 4 -> '  ab'). Step 5's "check by hand that every `export function` name in index.js appears as a README.md section heading" also restates Check 3's PASS condition (each exported name has a heading). The criterion lets the builder write its own tests. It does not let the builder brief carry a probe, meaning inputs with expected outputs, that also appears in the verifier brief. So the builder brief contains part of the checker's bar.
